chunks.section: Product Certification Process & Grant of Licence
chunks.chunk_text: - Scheme Overview: BIS operates Product Certification Scheme (Scheme-I) under BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 for grant of licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). - Online Application: Manufacturers must register and apply through the official Manakonline e-portal (manakonline.in) along with application fee and required documents. - Infrastructure Prerequisites: The manufacturing unit must have necessary manufacturing machinery, complete in-house testing facilities as per Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), and qualified technical quality control personnel.

chunks.section: Certification Pathways: Normal vs Simplified Procedure
chunks.chunk_text: 1. Normal Procedure (Option 1): - Preliminary factory audit conducted by BIS officers. - Verification of manufacturing infrastructure, quality control system, and in-house testing laboratory. - Drawing of official verification samples during audit for testing in BIS recognized laboratory. - Grant of CM/L (Certification Mark Licence) upon receiving passing test reports and compliance with SIT. 2. Simplified Procedure (Option 2): - Available for select products where applicant gets sample pre-tested from a BIS-recognized testing laboratory. - Application submitted with pre-testing report, factory layout, and manufacturing details. - Licence granted after verification of application documents and factory audit, reducing grant timeline.

- Once granted, licence is valid for 1 to 2 years and renewable upon payment of marking fees. - Licensees must follow the prescribed Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT) and maintain routine test records. - BIS conducts unannounced periodic factory surveillance audits and draws market surveillance samples from retail channels to ensure continuous compliance. - Misuse of ISI mark or selling non-conforming goods is a cognizable offense under Section 29 of the BIS Act, 2016.

chunks.section: BIS Hallmarking & HUID — Initial Ingestion Notes
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS public information.

https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/hallmarking-faqs/hallmarking-faq/ Current official FAQ facts to index: - HUID means Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number. - HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric number and is unique for each hallmarked item. - Consumers can verify HUID using the BIS Care App's "Verify HUID" feature. - BIS states that, since the introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, hallmark on gold jewellery consists of three marks: BIS logo, purity of the article in caratage and fineness, and six-digit alphanumeric HUID number.

https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/consumer-protection/?lang=en BIS states that: - Consumers can have jewellery/sample tested at BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centres on a chargeable basis. - BIS provides guidance concerning testing and compensation in cases where hallmarked jewellery is found to have lower purity than declared. - HUID authenticity can be checked through the BIS Care App.

chunks.section: BIS Gold Hallmarking & HUID Official Guidelines
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/hallmarking-faqs/hallmarking-faq/?lang=en

- Governing Standard: IS 1417 — Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking — Specification. - Mandatory Implementation: Under the Hallmarking Order, mandatory hallmarking on gold jewellery came into effect on 1 July 2021 in designated districts and has been progressively expanded across India. - Exemption Threshold: Certain items like export articles, lightweight items below 2 grams, and medical/industrial items have specific statutory exemptions as per BIS notifications.

chunks.section: The 3 Mandatory Hallmarks on Gold Jewellery
chunks.chunk_text: Since 1 July 2021, hallmark on gold jewellery consists of three mandatory marks: 1. BIS Logo (Triangle Hallmark). 2. Purity of the article in Caratage & Fineness (24K999, 23K958, 22K916, 20K833, 18K750, 14K585). 3. 6-digit Alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) code unique to each piece.

- HUID is a 6-digit unique alphanumeric code laser-inscribed on each item at BIS-recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs). - The HUID links the item in the central BIS digital registry to the manufacturing jeweller, the AHC that tested it, date of hallmarking, and exact purity grade. - Violations, sale of fake hallmarks, or selling unhallmarked gold in mandatory districts attract penalties under Section 29 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016.

- Consumers should verify HUID authenticity using the 'Verify HUID' feature on the BIS Care App before purchasing. - Consumers can also have their jewellery tested at BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centres on a chargeable basis. - If hallmarked jewellery is found to have lower purity than declared, BIS guidelines mandate that the jeweller must pay compensation to the buyer equal to two times the shortfall calculated on the purchase value.

chunks.section: BIS Silver Hallmarking — Official Guidelines & IS 2112:2025
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS / Press Information Bureau public information. Official source URL: https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2050123 BIS Portal: https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/

- Governing Standard: IS 2112:2025 (superseding IS 2112:2014) — Silver and Silver Alloys — Fineness and Marking — Specification. - Implementation Status: The Hallmarking Unique Identification (HUID)-based hallmarking for silver jewellery and artefacts was introduced on a voluntary basis effective from 1 September 2025. - Alignment with Gold: The revised IS 2112:2025 standard aligns silver hallmarking with the gold hallmarking architecture by introducing digital traceability via a 6-digit alphanumeric HUID code.

chunks.section: Recognized Purity Grades (Fineness in parts per 1000)
chunks.chunk_text: The revised Indian Standard IS 2112:2025 specifies seven permitted purity grades for silver jewellery and artefacts: 1. 999 (99.9% pure silver — newly added in IS 2112:2025) 2. 990 (99.0% pure silver) 3. 970 (97.0% pure silver) 4. 958 (95.8% pure silver — newly added in IS 2112:2025) 5. 925 (92.5% pure silver — standard Sterling Silver) 6. 835 (83.5% pure silver) 7. 800 (80.0% pure silver)

chunks.section: The 3 Mandatory Marks on Hallmarked Silver
chunks.chunk_text: Under IS 2112:2025, every hallmarked silver article must be laser-inscribed with three distinct marks: 1. BIS Standard Mark featuring the explicit word "SILVER". 2. Purity / Fineness Grade (one of the 7 official grades, e.g., 925, 999). 3. 6-digit Alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) code unique to each piece.

chunks.section: Consumer Verification via BIS Care App
chunks.chunk_text: - Consumers can verify the authenticity, declared purity grade, jewellery category, date of hallmarking, and registered jeweller / Assaying and Hallmarking Centre (AHC) details by entering the 6-digit HUID code into the official "BIS CARE" mobile application under the "Verify HUID" feature. - Consumers can also get their silver jewellery tested for purity on a chargeable basis at any BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre.

chunks.section: BIS Care App & Consumer Verification Guide
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/bis-apps/?lang=en Consumer Protection Portal: https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/consumer-protection/?lang=en

The official 'BIS CARE' mobile app (available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store) provides essential citizen-centric transparency and verification features: 1. Verify Licence Details (CM/L): Enter the 7-digit or 8-digit CM/L license number displayed on any ISI-marked product to check validity, manufacturer name, brand name, address, and applicable Indian Standard. 2. Verify Registration Details (CRS): Enter the 'R-XXXXXXXX' registration number on electronic and IT goods to check validity and manufacturing details. 3. Verify HUID: Enter the 6-digit alphanumeric code laser-inscribed on hallmarked gold and silver jewellery to view jewellery type, purity grade, jeweller name, and hallmarking centre. 4. Know Your Standards: Search Indian Standards, view scope summaries, recent amendments, and gazette notifications. 5. Locate Testing Laboratories: Find nearest BIS recognized laboratories and assaying & hallmarking centres.

- Consumers can lodge grievances directly through the BIS Care App or the consumer portal for: - Misuse of BIS Standard Mark (ISI mark) without a valid license. - Misleading quality claims on uncertified goods. - Substandard hallmarking or incorrect purity on jewellery. - Shortfall in product performance compared to Indian Standard specifications. - Complaints can include geo-tagged photos, invoices, and product packaging details for enforcement action by BIS surveillance officers.

- Consumers can submit hallmarked jewellery items to any BIS Recognized Assaying and Hallmarking Centre for independent testing upon payment of nominal testing fees. - If testing shows lower purity than the declared hallmark grade, the jeweller is legally obligated under BIS regulations to pay compensation equal to two times the shortfall calculated on the purchase value of the article.
Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/system-certification-overview/systems-under-certification/?lang=en

The Bureau of Indian Standards operates management systems certification schemes for organizations across multiple industrial and service sectors. These certifications demonstrate compliance with international standards: 1. Quality Management System (QMS) — IS/ISO 9001: Demonstrates consistent ability to provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory requirements. 2. Environmental Management System (EMS) — IS/ISO 14001: Provides a framework for protecting the environment and responding to changing environmental conditions. 3. Food Safety Management System (FSMS) — IS/ISO 22000: Ensures food safety throughout the food chain up to the point of consumption. 4. Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) — IS/ISO 45001: Improves workplace safety and reduces employee risks. 5. Information Security Management System (ISMS) — IS/ISO/IEC 27001: Secures organizational information assets and data confidentiality. 6. Energy Management System (EnMS) — IS/ISO 50001: Enables organizations to establish systems and processes to improve energy efficiency. 7. Medical Devices Quality Management System (MDQMS) — IS/ISO 13485: Specific requirements for regulatory compliance of medical device manufacturers.

- Application: Submission of organization profile, system manual, and applicable standard. - Stage 1 Audit: Off-site and on-site review of management system documentation, adequacy of policies, and readiness for Stage 2. - Stage 2 Audit: Comprehensive on-site audit evaluating implementation, operational control, and effectiveness of the management system. - Certification Decision: Grant of license upon satisfactory resolution of non-conformities (NCs). - Surveillance & Recertification: Periodic surveillance audits conducted every year, with complete recertification every 3 years.

chunks.section: BIS Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) FAQ
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/fmcs/fmcs-faqs/?lang=en

- Scheme Basis: FMCS operates under Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the Bureau of Indian Standards (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. - Purpose: Grants licence to foreign manufacturers located outside India to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on products exported to the Indian market. - Scope: Covers both voluntary standards and products notified under Compulsory Quality Control Orders (QCOs) by Government of India ministries.

1. Authorized Indian Representative (AIR): - Every foreign applicant must nominate an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) who is an Indian resident or an entity incorporated in India. - The AIR is legally responsible for compliance with the BIS Act, 2016, rules, regulations, and terms of the license agreement. 2. In-house Manufacturing & Testing Facility: - The foreign manufacturing unit must have independent manufacturing facilities and complete testing equipment as per the relevant Indian Standard. 3. Factory Audit by BIS Officers: - BIS technical officers visit the manufacturing premises abroad to audit manufacturing infrastructure, test facilities, quality control systems, and draw verification samples. 4. Independent Testing in India: - Verification samples drawn during the foreign factory inspection are tested in BIS recognized laboratories in India. 5. Financial Compliance: - Upon successful verification, the foreign manufacturer must submit a Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) and pay applicable marking fees prior to license grant.

chunks.section: BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) — Scheme II
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/?lang=en CRS Portal: https://www.crsbis.in/BIS/

- Conformity Model: Self-declaration of conformity scheme governed under Scheme-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. - Applicability: Primarily covers Electronic, Information Technology (IT), and Solar Photovoltaic goods notified under Compulsory Registration Orders (CRO) by MeitY and MNRE. - Common Products: Laptops, Tablets, Mobile Phones, Power Banks, Smart Watches, LED Luminaires, Power Adapters, Point of Sale (POS) terminals, and Lithium-ion Secondary Cells.

chunks.section: Key Process Distinction: No Initial Factory Audit
chunks.chunk_text: - Unlike Scheme-I (ISI Mark), Scheme-II does NOT require an on-site factory audit prior to registration. - Testing Requirement: The manufacturer gets product models tested in a BIS-recognized testing laboratory located in India. - Test Report Validity: Test reports submitted for registration must not be older than 90 days from the date of issue. - Grant of Registration: Upon online submission of valid test report, undertaking of compliance, and fee, BIS issues a unique Registration Number.

- Products registered under Scheme-II carry the standard words: 'Self-Declaration — Conforming to IS [Number]' along with the BIS Registration Number 'R-XXXXXXXX' and the official BIS portal reference (www.bis.gov.in). - Selling, distributing, or importing non-registered notified electronic goods into India is prohibited by law under the MeitY QCO orders.

chunks.section: BIS Certificate of Conformity (CoC) — Scheme IV
chunks.chunk_text: Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-4/?lang=en

- Regulatory Basis: Governed under Scheme-IV of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. - Purpose: Provides a conformity assessment mechanism for products or consignments where granting a continuous manufacturing licence (Scheme-I) is not feasible or applicable. - Applicability: Typically applied to limited manufacturing runs, batch/consignment imports, components, or specialized items governed by statutory notifications.

1. Application: Manufacturer or importer applies with batch details, invoice, packing list, and specifications. 2. Sampling & Inspection: BIS draws representative samples from the specific consignment or manufacturing batch. 3. Laboratory Testing: Drawn samples are tested against relevant Indian Standard specifications in a BIS-approved laboratory. 4. Grant of CoC: A Certificate of Conformity is issued strictly covering the verified batch quantity upon passing laboratory tests.

Source status: Official BIS Public Information. Official source URL: https://www.bis.gov.in/scheme-x-certification/faq-scheme-x-certification/?lang=en Scheme X Portal: https://www.scheme-x.bis.gov.in/

- Regulatory Basis: Scheme-X is an advanced conformity assessment scheme notified under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. - Target Sectors: Applicable to manufacturers of heavy industrial machinery, low-voltage switchgear and controlgear, transformers, rotating electrical machines, and complex industrial equipment. - Global Scope: Applicable to both domestic Indian manufacturers and foreign manufacturers exporting industrial equipment to India.

1. Product Testing: Comprehensive type-testing of product prototypes at BIS recognized or accredited testing laboratories. 2. Technical File Evaluation: Detailed engineering review of design drawings, quality assurance manuals, bill of materials, and safety risk assessments. 3. Factory Audit: Audit of manufacturer quality control systems, production capability, and in-house inspection protocols. 4. Scheme-X License: Grant of certificate allowing the application of Scheme-X Standard Mark for the certified industrial equipment series.
